overview: Reddit operates a network of ~100,000+ topic-based communities ('subreddits') built on user-generated text, image, and video content and threaded discussion, with ~515M weekly and 130.3M daily active uniques (DAUq) as of Q3 2026 (US 50.7M, International 79.6M). It monetizes primarily through auction-based digital advertising (Reddit Ads, including the automated 'Reddit Max' stack, ~95% of revenue) and, secondarily, through data-licensing/API agreements with AI companies (Google, OpenAI and others) that train and ground LLMs on Reddit's human conversation corpus. Reddit IPO'd in March 2024, joined the S&P 500 in 2026, passed $3B of trailing-12-month revenue in Q3 2026, and is now confronting a sharp slowdown in Google search-referral traffic that is flattening US users and forcing a pivot to a primarily logged-in experience.

business_model.summary: Advertising is the core revenue engine (~95% of revenue), sold as a performance/DR-focused auction (Reddit Ads, Reddit Max automated buying) alongside brand advertising. 'Other revenue' (~5%, $48M in Q3 2026, +35% YoY) is data licensing/API fees from AI companies; contract-based but lumpy and subject to renewal/renegotiation (Google and OpenAI deals reportedly ~$60M and ~$70M/yr and up for renewal). Ad revenue is transactional; users are a free consumer base (B2B2C for ads, direct B2B for licensing). Gross margin 91.5%, Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 44.9%, capex only ~0.1% of revenue.
business_model.customer_type: B2B advertisers (SMB self-serve to large brand/agency) for ads; B2B AI/tech companies (Google, OpenAI, and others) for data licensing. Redditors are the free consumer base that generates content and traffic; management says logged-in and app users drive >80% of monetization.
business_model.geographic_mix: Q3 2026: US $719M (~80% of revenue, +50% YoY, ARPU $13.82 +53%), International $176M (~20%, +67% YoY, ARPU $2.43 +32%). DAUq mix is the reverse: US 50.7M (-2% YoY) vs International 79.6M (+24%), so international is under-monetized but US users are now shrinking.

main_competitors: AI chatbots (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity) as substitutes for forum search
competitive_position.market_position: Category-defining player in threaded, topic-based community discussion; positioned as a core 'ground truth' human-content source for generative AI, a role largely unique among consumer platforms. However, AI answer engines are increasingly intermediating the search traffic that fed Reddit's growth.

moat_factors.description: Value of each subreddit compounds with contributors and moderators; 17+ years of archived threads make communities self-sustaining and hard to replicate.

Large, authentic, continuously refreshed conversational corpus is scarce and valuable for AI training/grounding; Reddit is litigating (Anthropic) and moving toward logged-in access partly to protect it from scraping. Leverage depends on AI labs continuing to value it, which the unresolved Google renewal tests.
Karma, moderator status and history create stickiness for logged-in users, but the ~59% of DAUq that is logged-out (largely search-referred) has low switching costs.
Historically Reddit's growth engine via Google ranking; now a liability as AI Overviews/AI Mode divert clicks (referrals reportedly fell by more than 1M per week in October 2026).
Widely recognized, now S&P 500 member with >$3B TTM revenue, but far smaller in ad dollars and engagement than Meta, Google or TikTok.

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on Google search referrals for new-user acquisition; management now says AI Overviews/AI Mode are driving a decline that could cut Q4 DAUq by a low double-digit percent from ~130M
US DAUq now shrinking (-2% YoY; logged-out US -4%), and US logged-in only +1%
Planned shift to a primarily logged-in experience will trade reach for engagement and carries execution risk
Data licensing concentrated in a few counterparties (Google, OpenAI) with unresolved renewals; management says it may not do a deal if terms do not suit its strategy
Smaller, less mature ad stack than Meta/Google/TikTok, though Reddit Max and lower-funnel formats are ramping quickly
Volunteer-run moderation creates governance and quality risk

growth_drivers: Ad-stack maturation: Reddit Max adoption more than tripled QoQ in Q3 2026; lower-funnel shopping and app-install revenue grew >95%; upper-funnel video revenue more than doubled
ARPU expansion: global ARPU $6.87 (+36%), US ARPU $13.82 (+53%) -- monetization is outgrowing user growth, and logged-in/app users carry the bulk of revenue
International expansion: international revenue +67% YoY, DAUq +24%, ARPU only ~18% of US; machine translation extends non-English content

Logged-in transition: tests starting in select non-US markets in Q4 2026, aimed at better ad targeting, scrape protection and regulatory compliance; management expects logged-in/app DAUq to converge toward total DAUq
Data licensing and AI partnerships: active discussions with AI partners, pushing usage-based rather than flat-fee pricing (no update provided; Anthropic suit supports pricing leverage)
Reddit Answers / on-platform search and shopping surfaces to monetize high-intent queries and build direct habit
Operating leverage and capital return: 44.9% adj. EBITDA margin, FCF $363M in Q3, $3.03B cash and securities, ~$660M left on buyback authorization

business.risk: Google search referral decline / AI Overviews
business.description: CEO said referrals fell by more than 1M per week in October and Q4 DAUq could fall by a low double-digit percent from 130M if the trend persists; attributed to AI Overviews and AI Mode. Logged-out DAUq (59% of total) is most exposed.
US DAUq -2% YoY, US WAUq flat, US logged-in +1%. US is ~80% of revenue, so ARPU growth must carry the model.
Making Reddit primarily logged-in could reduce reach and traffic before engagement and targeting gains materialize; management acknowledges a likely reach-for-engagement trade-off.
CFO said some Q3 bookings could not be delivered on certain September days; reduced inventory from falling traffic could cap ad growth. Competes for budgets with Meta, Google, TikTok, Amazon.
Quality and trust depend on unpaid third-party moderators.

financial.description: SBC guided to low-to-mid-teens % of revenue for FY2026. Buybacks ($100M in Q3, $340M YTD) are keeping fully diluted shares roughly flat (206.3M, -0.3% QoQ) rather than shrinking them.
~95% of revenue is cyclical ad spend; the data-licensing line is small (~$48M/qtr) and may not offset ad weakness.
Shares have fallen sharply in 2026 (reported near $92 after the Q3 print versus ~$141-165 in July-August); balance sheet is strong (no debt) but multiple is sensitive to user trends.

regulatory.description: UK Online Safety Act age assurance, EU DSA and US state/federal child-safety laws raise compliance cost and can add friction; management cites regulatory adaptation as one reason for the logged-in move.
Evolving Section 230-adjacent debates could raise compliance costs or constrain moderation discretion.

regulatory.risk: AI training-data law and litigation outcomes
regulatory.description: Reddit's breach-of-contract suit against Anthropic (remanded to California state court March 2026; judge sounded skeptical of Anthropic at an August 12, 2026 hearing) is a potential positive, but adverse preemption rulings or privacy rules on training data could weaken licensing leverage.

macro.description: Advertiser budgets are discretionary; a downturn would hit the core revenue line, especially with decelerating growth (Q4 guide implies 38-42% vs 53% in Q3).
Data licensing depends on AI labs' willingness to pay; synthetic data, in-house collection or hardball renewal negotiations could pressure that revenue.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Digital advertising continues to grow, with performance/DR formats and AI-optimized buying taking share. Search is being restructured by generative AI answer engines, reducing referral traffic to publishers and communities while raising the value of owned, logged-in audiences and proprietary data.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high -- advertising is discretionary and cyclical; data licensing is contract-based and less cyclical but subject to renewal risk.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity: no debt and $3.03B cash and marketable securities at Sept 30, 2026. Indirect sensitivity through ad-spend cyclicality and growth-stock multiples.
key_input_costs: Cloud/data-center infrastructure and AI inference costs (cost of revenue; gross margin 91.5%)
Content delivery and trust & safety operations

recent_developments.event: Q3 2026 results: revenue $895.0M (+53% YoY, above $860-870M guide), ad revenue $847M (+54%), other revenue $48M (+35%), net income $283M, diluted EPS $1.40, adj. EBITDA $402M (44.9%), FCF $363M. DAUq 130.3M (+12%; US 50.7M -2%, Intl 79.6M +24%), ARPU $6.87 (+36%).

Q4 2026 guidance of revenue $1.00-1.03B (+38-42% YoY) and adj. EBITDA $480-510M. CEO warned October search referrals fell by more than 1M per week and Q4 DAUq could drop by a low double-digit percent from ~130M if the trend continues, blaming Google AI Overviews/AI Mode. Stock reported down ~29% to ~$92 the next session (cause not itemized in the source).

Management announced a plan to become primarily logged-in (tests in select non-US markets in Q4) to improve targeting, protect the corpus from scraping and adapt to regulation; acknowledged reach-for-engagement trade-off. Reddit stopped breaking out US logged-in DAUq as a headline metric earlier in the year.
Reddit added to the S&P 500; TTM revenue surpassed $3B. Repurchased ~670K shares for $100M (avg ~$149.81) in Q3, $340M YTD, ~$660M authorization remaining; fully diluted shares 206.3M.

Data licensing: management in active talks with AI partners, no update; said it may not strike a deal if terms do not serve strategy. Google (~$60M/yr) and OpenAI (~$70M/yr, est.) renewals remain unresolved after July WSJ reports that Reddit weighed restricting Google's access.

California state court hearing in Reddit v. Anthropic (breach of contract over scraping); judge reportedly skeptical of Anthropic's preemption argument. Case had been remanded to state court on March 31, 2026.

Q2 2026 results beat (revenue $804.9M +61%, DAUq 130.3M +18%) but stock fell ~11-20% on 'choppy' search referrals; JPMorgan cut target to $185 (neutral), Wedbush to $221 (outperform), Cantor to $170 (neutral); mid-August consensus target ~ $215.
Reports that Reddit may not renew or may tighten its Google AI licensing deal; stock fell ~8-9%.

items.notes: Implies 38-42% YoY growth, a clear deceleration from 53% in Q3 and 61% in Q2. Q3 beat the prior $860-870M guide.
Implies roughly 48-50% margin at guided revenue, above Q3's 44.9%.
Conditional on October search-referral declines (>1M/week) continuing; not formal guidance.
No change identified in the Q3 materials reviewed.
Active discussions with AI partners, no updates; may forgo deals that do not fit strategy.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Steve Huffman attributed the search-referral decline mainly to Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode pushing traffic away from external sites, and said the answer is a primarily logged-in, app-centric Reddit; logged-in and app users already drive over 80% of monetization and he expects logged-in/app DAUq to converge with total DAUq. Reddit Max adoption more than tripled QoQ and lower-funnel revenue grew >95%. Acquisitions for user growth are not a priority; focus is new-user retention, incognito mode to curb reinstalls, and converting mobile web to app. The CFO noted some Q3 bookings could not be delivered on certain September days.

bull_case: Monetization is still compounding: Q3 revenue +53%, US ARPU +53%, 44.9% adj. EBITDA margin, and Q4 guide implies EBITDA margin near 50%, so earnings power is growing even if users dip

Logged-in/app users already drive >80% of monetization, so losing low-value logged-out search traffic may hurt revenue less than headline DAUq suggests; logged-in transition builds a durable owned audience
Ad stack is scaling quickly (Reddit Max usage >3x QoQ, shopping/app-install +95%, video >2x) with a long international ARPU runway (Intl ARPU ~18% of US)
Scarce human-conversation corpus gives AI-licensing optionality and legal leverage (Anthropic suit); renewals at usage-based pricing could be a catalyst
Fortress balance sheet ($3.03B cash and securities, no debt, ~$660M buyback capacity) and a sharply de-rated share price after the October selloff
bear_case: Google AI Overviews/AI Mode are structurally eroding the search referral funnel; management itself flags a possible low-double-digit DAUq drop in Q4, and the effect may persist rather than reverse
US DAUq is now declining (-2% YoY) while the US generates ~80% of revenue, so growth leans on ARPU and ad load that has limits; revenue growth is decelerating from 61% to 53% to a 38-42% guide
Pivot to a primarily logged-in experience is untested and could cost reach and top-of-funnel growth before targeting benefits show up
Data-licensing revenue (~5% of sales) is concentrated in Google and OpenAI with unresolved renewals; Reddit may lose or reprice deals, and AI labs may favor synthetic or alternative data
Rising regulatory/compliance load (age verification, DSA, child safety) and volunteer moderation add friction and cost, while buybacks only offset SBC dilution rather than shrinking the share count
analysis_note_2026_10_31: Q3-2026 (reported 2026-10-29): revenue $895.0M (+53%), net income $283.3M, FCF $362.6M, DAUq 130.3M (+12%; US -2%), ARPU $6.87 (+36%). The thesis has shifted from 'monetization outgrowing users' to 'can monetization keep outgrowing a shrinking, search-dependent user base': Q4 guide of $1.00-1.03B implies deceleration to 38-42% and management flagged possible low-double-digit DAUq declines on collapsing Google referrals. Stock reportedly fell ~29% post-print (per a Motley Fool page; not independently verified). Q4 guidance figures confirmed from the Q3 8-K press release; analyst reaction and post-print price targets were not found in web sources and are not included.
